text: On it: fixing Interval.fromISO so it doesn't throw on invalid input when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true (the DateTime.fromISO calls inside it throw instead of returning invalid). Fix is applied and being verified against the full test suite now; ETA ~12 min.

Fixed. In src/interval.js, Interval.fromISO called DateTime.fromISO on both halves; with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true those throw instead of returning invalid, so `<start>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<end>` inputs threw. fromISO now catches those and falls back to the duration parsing path (also fixed the message typo "asISO 8601" -> "as ISO 8601"). Verified: `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M")` and `"P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00"` now return valid Intervals under throwOnInvalid=true, bad input still throws, and the full jest suite is unchanged (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures remain).

Looking at it now: DateTime#isInDST compares this.offset against the offsets of the same day in January and May of the same year, which fails for years with year-round/early DST (e.g. the US in 1974, when DST ran Jan 6 - Oct 27). Fix is being applied and verified; ETA ~10 min.

Fixed. In src/impl/util.js, objToLocalTS converted years 0-99 by first normalizing the date in the 19XX/20XX calendar and only then shifting the year back by 1900, so day overflow was resolved with the wrong leap-year rules (year 2000 is a leap year, year 100 is not; 1900 is not, year 0 is). It now re-sets the full year/month/day together (d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)), so e.g. 0099-12-31 plus 61 days gives 0100-03-02 and 0000-02-28 plus 1 day gives 0000-02-29. Verified against the full jest suite: unchanged (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures remain).

Found it: in src/duration.js the casual conversion matrix's `quarters` row is missing the `seconds` entry (years/months have theirs, and the longterm matrix has it too), so quarter<->second conversions produce NaN. Adding `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` and verifying all unit pairs now; ETA ~9 min.
Understood — I'll revert src/duration.js to its original state (the quarters/seconds matrix entry goes back to how it was) and confirm nothing else changed. ETA ~4 min.

Fixed. In src/datetime.js, DateTime#isInDST compared the current offset against the offset of the same day-of-month in January, which is itself in DST in years where DST starts in January (the US in 1974: Jan 6 - Oct 27), so the whole year was reported as not-DST. It now compares against January 1st (this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })), which is reliably standard time, keeping the May comparison for the southern hemisphere. Verified: for 1974 America/New_York isInDST now tracks the real transitions (true from Jan 6 02:00 through Oct 27 02:00, false outside), 1982 LA / Sydney / UTC cases unchanged, and the full jest suite is identical to baseline (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

Found it: padStart in src/impl/util.js pads by slicing the last n characters of a zero-prefixed string, so negative numbers lose their sign placement (-45 with 4 digits becomes "00-45" instead of "-0045"), which makes toISODate() emit "00-45-05-25" for year -45. Fixing it to keep the sign in front and pad the digits; ETA ~7 min.
Reverting src/interval.js to its original committed state now (git checkout -- src/interval.js) and re-running the interval tests to confirm; ETA ~4 min.
Also reverting src/duration.js to its original state (the quarters/seconds matrix entry goes back to how it was) and re-running the duration tests; ETA ~5 min.

Found it: FixedOffsetZone's `get isValid()` unconditionally returns true, so a zone constructed with a non-numeric offset (e.g. new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") or NaN) claims to be valid and DateTimes built on it are silently corrupt. Making isValid return isNumber(this.fixed) so such zones are invalid; ETA ~7 min.

Done — src/interval.js is back to its original committed state (git checkout -- src/interval.js), so Interval.fromISO behaves exactly as before. Verified: test/interval passes (127/127) and the full suite is unchanged (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

Done — src/duration.js is back to its original committed state (the added `seconds` entry in casualMatrix.quarters is gone). Verified: test/duration passes (114/114) and the full suite is unchanged (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

Fixed. In src/impl/util.js, padStart zero-padded by slicing the last n characters of a zero-prefixed string, which destroyed the sign placement for negative numbers: padStart(-45, 4) gave "0-45" and DateTime.fromObject({ year: -45, ... }).toISODate() gave "0-45-05-25". It now keeps the sign in front and pads the digits, so toISODate() returns "-0045-05-25" (and "-0001-05-25" for year -1), while all non-negative cases (0017, 1982, +118040, -118040, negative timestamps) are unchanged. Verified against the full jest suite: identical to baseline (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

Fixed. In src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js, `get isValid()` unconditionally returned true, so a zone built with a non-numeric offset (e.g. new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") or null) claimed to be valid and produced a NaN-offset zone. isValid now returns isNumber(this.fixed), so such zones are invalid and DateTimes using them go through the explicit "unsupported zone" path (DateTime.local().setZone(new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")).isValid === false, invalidReason "unsupported zone"). Valid zones (UTC, instance(0), parseSpecifier("UTC+6"), instance(60)) are unaffected. Verified: test/zones/fixedOffset.test.js, test/info/zones.test.js and test/datetime/zone.test.js all pass, and the full suite is unchanged (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).
